# Project Memories

> Durable cross-session knowledge for Rocky Surf, migrated from the maintainers' internal
> `bd remember` notes. Each entry below is self-contained; read the linked file for the full
> story.
>
> These are lessons and rulings that outlived the session that produced them — not a changelog
> and not a task tracker. For decisions about the shape of the software itself, see the ADRs in
> `docs/adr/` instead; a memory here may point at one.
>
> Every entry here is `active`. A memory that gets superseded is removed from this index rather
> than left to mislead in place.

## Engineering practice

- [orchestrating-issue-agent-teams](2026-08-26-orchestrating-issue-agent-teams.md): how one
  session closed twenty issues with a team of worktree-isolated agents — triage by component,
  model per issue, a shared brief, four concurrent, ≤12-line reports, and what to do when
  GitHub Actions is down.
- [plain-spoken-pr-comments](2026-08-30-plain-spoken-pr-comments.md): owner ruling (#251):
  every agent-opened PR gets a plain-spoken comment — what it does, what merging changes, what
  the human must do, what it costs — and required setup ships as a run-one-script, never as
  copy/paste steps.
- [setup-scripts-verify-what-they-claimed](2026-08-31-setup-scripts-verify-what-they-claimed.md):
  issue #270 — the Azure nightly's federated credential was fixed and still missing, because the
  step that made it had an `else` branch that carried on. A wiring step gets no fallback, and the
  script reads the state back and compares it with what the other side will send.
- [keep-both-merge-gate-rule](2026-08-13-keep-both-merge-gate-rule.md): a keep-both merge conflict
  resolution can produce syntax damage no marker scan or diff review will catch — run the full
  quality gate after every one.
- [whole-boot-wiring-tests](2026-08-21-whole-boot-wiring-tests.md): passing unit tests per module
  can coexist with a product that can't boot — add a whole-boot wiring test at every composition
  seam.
- [pnpm-sdk-build-race](2026-08-21-pnpm-sdk-build-race.md): how a shared-worktree build race used
  to produce failures that looked like real bugs, and the atomic-rename build fix that closed most
  of it.
- [verify-the-checkout-before-you-work](2026-08-26-verify-the-checkout-before-you-work.md): this
  machine has eleven worktrees and an archived remote that is easy to mistake for the live one — a
  stale checkout builds, tests green, and cannot be pushed. Check before editing, not at push time.
- [reject-whole-readers-need-validating-writers](2026-08-26-reject-whole-readers-need-validating-writers.md):
  the price-feed reader rejects a document whole on one bad price — correct, and it means one
  zero-priced vendor meter unpriced all of Azure everywhere while the publisher stayed green. A
  reject-whole consumer obliges its producer to validate with the same predicate.
- [regional-ubuntu-mirrors-fail-as-a-unit](2026-08-26-regional-ubuntu-mirrors-fail-as-a-unit.md):
  a cloud image's per-region Ubuntu mirror takes every box in the region down with it, and apt
  never retries a 503 at any `Acquire::*` setting — the bootstrap agent's mirror fallback is the
  remedy. Amended 2026-08-27 (#188): the fallback's retry is now per step, the global archive's
  own 404s need a wait rather than a different mirror, and Pack smoke runs the real `agent.sh`.
- [launchers-hand-the-agent-less-than-a-shell-does](2026-08-26-launchers-hand-the-agent-less-than-a-shell-does.md):
  the transient systemd unit gives the bootstrap agent no `HOME`, and every harness stood in
  for it with a shell that does — a harness must strip what the real launcher withholds, and
  the agent, not the launcher, establishes what the pack contract promises.

## Writing and documentation

- [measured-numbers-in-prose](2026-08-13-measured-numbers-in-prose.md): why a measurement of this
  repository needs exactly one dated, re-measured home instead of being copied into prose.
- [pass-along-home](2026-08-21-pass-along-home.md): session hand-off notes live in `.pass-along/`
  in this repository, and they're world-readable — no secrets, ever.

## Architecture

- [everyone-who-runs-an-installation-is-its-admin](2026-08-27-everyone-who-runs-an-installation-is-its-admin.md):
  owner ruling (#192): Rocky Surf is one engineer's own tooling, so there is no non-admin user to
  design for — `isAdmin` is a seam in the code, not a population. Never add a route or a second
  screen whose only justification is widening the audience; the `/admin/*` prefix and its
  middleware stay exactly as they are.
- [session-tokens-opaque-not-signed](2026-08-21-session-tokens-opaque-not-signed.md): why sessions
  are opaque random tokens validated by database lookup, not signed cookies.
- [vendor-sdk-vs-rest-provider-ruling](2026-08-13-vendor-sdk-vs-rest-provider-ruling.md): the test
  a new compute provider applies before taking a vendor SDK dependency — REST by hand by default,
  buy only the auth part when it's genuinely not fetch-shaped.

## Cloud providers

- [azure-core-quota-is-a-second-gate](2026-08-26-azure-core-quota-is-a-second-gate.md): Azure refuses
  a create twice — SKU restrictions, then per-family core quota — and a fresh subscription has most
  families at zero; read `locations/usages` (case-insensitive family join), show the reason, and
  never treat an unreadable quota as no quota.
- [branch-protection-and-pr-workflow](2026-08-31-branch-protection-and-pr-workflow.md): Main is PR-only
  on rockysurf and rockysurf-shop (protect-main rulesets); the exact branch→PR→auto-merge commands,
  which four checks are required and why path-filtered jobs must never be, and the shop index bot's
  deploy-key bypass.
- [surge-pack-image-budget](2026-09-01-surge-pack-image-budget.md): [active] Surge pack images are
  256×256 PNGs and the set must stay under the 512 KB bundle-assets test budget; resize with
  `sips -Z 256` before committing, and never fix a red test by raising the limit.
- [run-pack-url-checker](2026-09-01-run-pack-url-checker.md): [active] Run `pnpm run check:pack-urls`
  periodically and whenever creating a new official surge pack; it's deliberately non-gating, so it
  only helps if actually run — treat failures as leads, not automatic reds.
